title: Super Plot spec v1
description: A declarative chart: a chart type, tabular rows and the columns to encode. Limits: 50000 rows.

oneOf.title: Bar chart
oneOf.description: Compares a number across categories with one bar per category (grouped, stacked or 100% stacked). Comparing sizes across a handful to a few dozen categories, or parts of a whole per category (stacked). Use a line for ordered time; use a histogram to show how one measure is distributed; avoid for more than ~40 categories.

version.description: Spec format version. Only 1 exists; may be omitted.

data.description: Tabular rows: an array of flat objects, one per observation. Numbers must be numbers (or plain numeric strings).

title.description: Chart title. State the takeaway or the subject, not "Chart".

subtitle.description: One line of context under the title: unit, period, filter.

description.description: Long description for screen readers and agents. Generated from the data when omitted.

source.description: Source line shown small under the chart.

legend.description: Legend placement. `auto` hides it for a single series and picks a side from the available width.

tooltip.description: Show a hover tooltip (web binding only).

format.description: Value format: auto, compact, integer, percent (ratios, 0.25 shows as 25%), fixed:N, currency:CODE.

colors.description: Series (or slice/category) name to CSS colour, e.g. {"Revenue":"#2962FF"}. Hex, rgb(), hsl(), a colour name or var(--x). Unlisted series keep palette colours.

transform.description: Data steps run before the chart reads its columns, in order: filter, timeUnit, aggregate, sort, top. E.g. [{"timeUnit":{"field":"date","unit":"month","as":"month"}},{"aggregate":{"groupBy":["month"],"fields":{"revenue":"mean"}}}]. Column fields then refer to the output.

patterns.description: Default false. Add a texture per series to filled marks (bars, areas, slices, cells) so series stay apart without colour: colour-blind readers, greyscale print.

yLabel.description: Title of the vertical axis (include the unit).

annotations.description: Reference marks: {axis:"y", value:100, label:"Target"} draws a line; add `to` for a band.

facet.description: Split into small multiples: one panel per value of this column (at most 12), sharing axes, colours and one legend. (name of a column in data)

zoom.description: Default none. Let the viewer zoom and pan a continuous axis (web binding): Ctrl/⌘-scroll or pinch to zoom, drag to pan, double-click or 0 to reset. Scatter, line and area.

brush.description: Default none. Let the viewer drag out a range to select (web binding). The selection comes back as a filter step, ready for `transform`. With `zoom` too, Shift-drag pans.

x.description: Column holding the category of each bar. (name of a column in data)

y.description: Numeric column for bar length. Several columns give one series per column (wide-form data). (column name, or several for wide-form data)

series.description: Column that splits each category into series (long-form data). Not needed when `y` lists several columns. (name of a column in data)

stack.description: `none` groups series side by side, `stack` stacks them, `normalize` stacks to 100%.

orientation.description: Use `horizontal` for long category names or many categories.

sort.description: Order categories by their total. `none` keeps the data order (use it for ordered categories such as months).

labels.description: Print values on the bars. Keep off for dense charts; the tooltip carries the numbers.

line.description: Combo chart: numeric column(s) drawn as lines with points over vertical bars, on the same value axis (a target, an average). Ignored for horizontal and 100% stacked bars. (column name, or several for wide-form data)

yDomain.description: Fix the value axis range, e.g. [0, 100]. Bars should start at 0; only change it knowingly.

oneOf.title: Line chart
oneOf.description: Shows how one or more numbers change along an ordered x axis, usually time. Trends over time or any ordered numeric x, up to ~8 series. Use area for cumulative or part-to-whole over time, bar for comparing separate categories, scatter when both axes are measurements. For prices (OHLC, indicators, drawings) use Super Chart.

oneOf.title: Area chart
oneOf.description: A line chart with the area under it filled; stacked areas show how parts add up over time. Volume or cumulative quantity over time, and composition over time (`stack: "stack"` or `"normalize"`). Avoid overlapping unstacked areas for more than 2 series; use lines instead.

oneOf.title: Scatter plot
oneOf.description: Plots each row as a point by two numbers to show relationships, clusters and outliers; optional bubble size and trend line. Asking whether two measures move together, or finding outliers. Add `size` for a third measure (bubble), `series` for groups, `trend: "linear"` for the fit. Not for ordered time series (use line) or part-to-whole.

oneOf.title: Pie chart
oneOf.description: Shows each category's share of a whole as angles of a circle. Few (2-6) parts of one whole where the point is "who has the biggest share". Prefer a bar chart to compare sizes precisely or to show more than ~7 parts. Not for time or for values that do not add up to a whole.

oneOf.description: Summarises the distribution of a number for each group: median, quartiles, whiskers and outliers. Comparing the spread and centre of one measure across many groups, where overlaid histograms would be too busy. Needs ~10+ values per group to be meaningful.

oneOf.title: Radar chart
oneOf.description: Compares a few items across several measures on spokes around a centre; each item is a closed shape. Comparing 1-4 items across 4-10 measures that share one scale (skills, product scorecards). The shape is easy to read, exact values are not: use a bar chart when precision matters, and avoid it for measures on different scales or for many items.

oneOf.title: Treemap

oneOf.title: Sankey diagram
oneOf.description: Shows how a quantity flows between stages: bands between nodes, the band width is the amount. A quantity that splits and merges across stages (budget to departments, visitors to pages to outcomes, energy sources to uses). Flows must go one way (no loops). Not for a single split (use a pie or bar) or for more than about 30 nodes.

oneOf.title: Choropleth map
oneOf.description: Colours each region of a map by a number; raise regions by the value for a 3D view. Comparing a rate or share across countries, provinces or districts. Map rates (per person, percent), not raw totals, or big regions dominate. Needs region boundaries (geo). For exact ranking use a sorted bar chart.

oneOf.title: Bubble map
oneOf.description: Places a circle per row on a map by longitude/latitude (or region), sized by a number and coloured by group. Showing where things are and how big they are: cities, sites, events, stores. Totals belong here rather than on a choropleth. Tens of thousands of points are fine (the web binding switches renderer). Use `geo` only to draw land under the points.
